A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–K support comparison; pagination and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original hubness statistics, prediction accuracies and token-frequency correlations for five LLMs across three corpora, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports the same original LLM experiments and additionally presents k-occurrence results for the synthetic Gaussian illustration in Figure 1.

M1.justification: The probability-distance definition, representation comparisons and hubness-analysis procedure remain unchanged. No model architecture, training objective or algorithmic component is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bookcorpus, Pile10k and WikiText-103 contexts, with the same additional training-corpus frequency comparisons. Figure 1 retains the same three- and 300-dimensional Gaussian scenarios; its additional analysis does not expand data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The five evaluated LLMs and the Euclidean, normalized Euclidean and softmaxed-dot-product comparisons are retained. Expanded explanations of hubness-mitigation methods do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figure 1 extends the Gaussian illustration with k-occurrence and k-skewness measurements alongside distance distributions. This is a limited addition to that analysis; the LLM sample sizes, model configurations, checkpoints, k=10 and hub threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The added lower panel of Figure 1 directly illustrates how dimensionality relates to asymmetric nearest-neighbour relations and hubness. The existing training-checkpoint analyses and qualitative hub/neighbourhood examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional synthetic k-skewness values describe the data distribution rather than uncertainty in estimated results.

E6.justification: Figure 1 newly reports Gaussian k-skewness values of -0.04 in three dimensions and 12.27 in 300 dimensions. The LLM table values and qualitative examples remain unchanged. Figure 5 rearranges existing correlations without changing their values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1, its assumptions and the Appendix A proof are unchanged. The added statement that the theorem does not cover Euclidean or cosine comparisons clarifies its existing scope.

C1.justification: The three stated contributions remain: nonuniform probability distances avoid concentration, prediction hubs reflect context-sensitive token frequency, and other representation comparisons can produce nuisance hubs. The revised abstract foregrounds practical advice without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that identifying junk tokens and semantically unrelated neighbours relies entirely on qualitative observation. It also qualifies some nuisance-hub assertions, expands implications for embeddings, retrieval and interpretability, and identifies further work on frequent-token mechanisms.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly provides a repository link for experiment and plotting code. The NVIDIA A30 hardware, compute-time estimates, software versions and asset information in Appendices I–J are retained, despite relocation.

R1.justification: Six references are added concerning LLM-derived embeddings, representation geometry and frequent-token mechanisms, including LLM2Vec and Macocco et al. (2025). Several already-cited mitigation methods receive fuller explanations; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, Related Work, Section 4.3, conclusion and limitations receive localized rewrites and explanatory additions. The section hierarchy remains intact. Copyediting fixes some wording while introducing a few new typographical errors.

P2.justification: Plots throughout the main text and appendices are redrawn with revised proportions and larger labels, accompanied by substantial float reflow. Figure 1 gains a panel, and Table 2 clarifies its overall-accuracy heading. Figure 5 transposes its panel arrangement but incorrectly retains the old row/column description in its caption.

improvement.justification: The code pointer, clearer illustrations, more legible plots and explicit qualitative-evidence limitation modestly improve usability and transparency. Scientific validation remains largely unchanged. Figure 5's stale caption is a presentation regression, but its headers and Table 15 still identify the unchanged correlations, limiting the harm.
